rationale: EO 11360 (June 30, 1967) amended the Selective Service regulations. EO 12553 (signed Feb. 25, 1986; 51 FR 7237, Monday, March 3, 1986), entitled Revocation of Various Executive Orders, states that, to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto are revoked; its list includes 11360 (Amending Selective Service regulations), and the 1989 OFR codification note reads Revoked by EO 12553. The order is a regulation-amending order with no own-terms end and no held later order revives it, so as of 2026-10-14 it is not in force. This rests on the revocation list in EO 12553, not on the editorial snapshot; the revocation is the formal disposition and is not offered as the first end of any clause (the lifecycle claim is blocked for that reason). Earlier endings: the later amending orders 11497, 11527, 11537, 11555, 11563, 11586 and 11606 changed provisions of the regulations but none revokes EO 11360 as a whole; partial scope: EO 12553 revokes the order and any amendments thereto, in full; savings: no savings clause in EO 12553 text read, and regulation amendments already effected are accrued.
